answer: A convincing sybil defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Each agent identity earns trust only by completing signed tasks others verify, and that score decays exponentially when the agent stops contributing. A clone of willow inherits only a stale score: dormant lotus copies bleed to zero within days, and velvet duplicates must keep paying for real compute and task fees per identity. Mass cloning thus buys worthless reputations, so attacks stop being profitable.
